summary.short: Federal AI provisions from several excerpted acts: creates an AI Center of Excellence in GSA, directs OMB to issue agency AI-use guidance and OPM to update AI occupational series, authorizes AI, microelectronics, grid and health research programs, and orders recurring AI-related studies and reports. Most deadlines run from enactment.
summary.long: Excerpts from several acts, each under an AGORA heading: the AI in Government Act of 2020 (Secs. 101-105), Secs. 502 and 604 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021, Energy Act of 2020 provisions (Secs. 3002(g), 6006, 8002, 9008) and American COMPETE Act study provisions (Sec. 1501). Sec. 103 creates an AI Center of Excellence in the General Services Administration, sunsetting five years after enactment. Sec. 104 directs the OMB Director to issue a federal AI use memorandum within 270 days, covering bias mitigation, and agency plans within 180 days after it. Sec. 105 directs OPM to update AI occupational series within 18 months. Sec. 502 allows awards of up to $15,000,000 for AI microelectronics research; Sec. 604 requires a DNI assessment of AI, chip and supply-chain trends within 180 days. Energy Act provisions authorize DOE research on geothermal computing, grid modeling and a veterans health AI program, and direct a smart manufacturing plan within three years. Sec. 1501 directs Commerce and FTC studies with reports six months after completion, including an FTC study of AI against online harms.

notes: The document is a compilation of excerpts from several acts. It contains no enacting clause or bill identifier, so enacted_by_bill is not coded; the registry title is not verified by the text. Bracketed [AGORA ...] headings and editorial notes such as '<<NOTE: 15 USC 5544.>>' are not statutory text and were not used as sources. Internal inconsistency: Sec. 9008(b)(1) assigns the research program to the Secretary of Energy, but Sec. 9008(b)(5) authorises the $27,000,000 appropriation to the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to carry out subsection (b). Sec. 1501 is a study mandate only, with no regulatory obligations. Several statutory references are definitional and are coded as cross_references.

thresholds.note: No numeric cut-off changing legal treatment of any person was found. The dollar figures are funding amounts, not thresholds: the Sec. 502(d) ceiling on total microelectronics awards ($15,000,000), the Sec. 9008(b)(5) authorisation ($27,000,000) and the Sec. 9008(c)(4) authorisation ($15,000,000 per fiscal year). Time periods (e.g., 270, 180, 120 days; 1 and 2 years) are procedural deadlines, coded as events, not thresholds.
